# MCP route probe. devin 3000.3.22, Hermes v0.19.0 (2026.7.20).
# Captured 2026-07-31. Session uuids replaced with <REDACTED-UUID>.
#
# Establishes that Hermes-side tools ARE reachable through the Devin ACP
# backend — not via the shim's prompt-level <tool_call> contract (which the
# model never chooses; see replay-toolcall-probe.txt), but by exposing them as
# an MCP server that Devin calls through its own native tool loop.
#
# Setup:
#   devin mcp add looper-memory -- python3 probe_mcp_server.py   # from the
#     directory that will be the ACP session cwd — `devin mcp add` writes to a
#     *local project config* keyed to cwd, so the session must share it.
#   ./replay_acp.py --cwd "$PWD" --prompt-file <prompt asking for the tool>
#
# Two attempts failed first, and the failures are the useful part:
#
# 1. Passing the server inline via session/new's `mcpServers` param: Devin
#    spawned the process and completed the MCP handshake (the server logged
#    `initialize` + `notifications/initialized`), but never called tools/list,
#    and the model reported: "Server `looper-memory` not found in
#    configuration." Devin's own registry lookup does not pick up
#    session-scoped servers. Registering via `devin mcp add` is the path that
#    works.
#
# 2. With the server registered but the shim's stock permission handling:
#    tools/list fired and the model tried to call the tool, but Hermes's shim
#    hardcodes `{"outcome": "cancelled"}` for every session/request_permission,
#    so the call was rejected. Model output: "The store call was rejected (you
#    skipped it), so the note LOOPER-MCP-42 was not stored."
#
# Below: registered server + permission approved.

  [permission] options=['allow_once', 'allow_session', 'allow_always', 'allow_server_session', 'allow_server_always', 'switch_bypass', 'reject_once'] -> allow_once
  [update] tool_call_update
  [update] tool_call_update
  [update] tool_call_update
  [update] usage_update
session/prompt result: {"stopReason": "end_turn", "usage": {"totalTokens": 13969, "inputTokens": 13947, "outputTokens": 22, "cachedReadTokens": 13891}, "_meta": {"cognition.ai/userMessageId": "<REDACTED-UUID>"}}
--- collected text ---
Done. Stored the note `LOOPER-MCP-42` in Looper's persistent memory.

# MCP server's own log for the same run — the tool really executed with the
# right argument, end to end:
RECV initialize
RECV notifications/initialized
RECV tools/list
RECV tools/call
